findings.wholeGoalFit: The broad goal concerns chemical hazard potential and justified risk reduction without a laboratory-only restriction. A household scenario directly fits it. The addition is qualified to the HB source route and does not impose a new all-jurisdiction completion duty.
findings.originalDuties: Own comparisons against pinned canonical and P439 inputs confirm unchanged complete goal, old core expectation, both original laboratory cases, both axes and all coverage controls. Acid-splash reasoning and the fresh volatile-substance comparison remain required.
findings.hazardVersusExposure: Product properties are explicitly fictional irritation hazards. Open pouring/wringing creates possible skin/eye contact; accessible open storage adds possible child contact. Amount and procedure influence exposure without erasing properties. No actual accident or numerical injury probability is inferred.
findings.actionReasoning: The equal effectiveness of water-cloth for this specific light dirt is explicitly stipulated, so non-use of R is justified for this task without generalizing water as universally sufficient. R must still be closed/inaccessible. Opening a window does not fix open contact or storage. Conditional option C grants neither necessity, glove suitability nor permission for a real product.
findings.scientificCoherence: A water-based, non-readily-volatile model liquid may still produce inhalable droplets when sprayed. Mist is correctly distinguished from vapour; no unsupported toxic gas or real chemical formulation is invented. Eye/skin/respiratory pathways are consistent with the stipulated properties.
findings.materialCompleteness: Material includes explicit fictional product and use cards,200mL open-bowl baseline, persons and access, stated alternative effectiveness, A/B/C options, learner task, reasoned response, fresh variation and task/response, four rubric criteria and blank learner fields. Data needed for qualitative judgment are supplied; no quantitative hazard class or risk score is required.
findings.freshTransfer: The same substance changes from unsprayed open-liquid handling to pump spraying above eye level in a poorly ventilated room. Learner must add droplet inhalation and face/eye contact, reject small-quantity means zero-risk and goggles solve everything, keep storage controls and justify the unchanged suitable non-use alternative. This is meaningful transfer of exposure reasoning rather than a new product-name recall.
findings.bilingualEquivalence: DE and EN preserve the same givens, duties, source scope, route distinctions, qualitative inference limits and prohibition on practical execution.
findings.safeAndTruthfulProspectiveState: No actual cleaning, spraying, substance preparation or dangerous learner execution is requested. R and its cards are fictional assumptions, not a product, certificate, SDS or authorization. Learner fields are blank and no action was observed.
findings.quota: Existing minimum/fresh/independent-transfer controls are unchanged; the added household reasoning creates no arbitrary count of real actions, files or chemicals.
